## 2. Construction of the action

The goal of this section is to perform the the following:

#### 2.0.0 Construction.

Let $Z$ be a quasi-smooth scheme. Then $\mathrm{IndCoh}(Z)$ receives a canonical action of $\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(Z))^{\Rightarrow}$ .

The outline of this section is as follows:

- – In §2.1 we briefly review material about sheaves of categories from [Gai15].

- – In §2.2 we describe a general construction for equipping a category with the structure of left module over the shearing of a symmetric monoidal category acted on by ${\mathbf{G}_{m}}$ . This construction is a sort of deperiodization result.

- – In §2.3 we apply the framework of §2.2 to carry out Construction 2.0.0, modulo the technical result Proposition 2.3.4. The main geometric input is that the vector space $V$ is open in $\mathbf{P}(V\oplus\mathbf{1})$ , which allows us to reduce to the results of [AG18].

- – In §2.4 we prove a “rigidity” theorem for relative crystals of categories, which gives us control over homotopy coherence problems.

- – In §2.5 we apply the framework of §2.4 to prove Proposition 2.3.4.

### 2.1. Review of sheaves of categories

#### 2.1.1.

For a morphism $f:T\to S$ of affine schemes, we will write

$$ \mathbf{ind}:\mathrm{QCoh}(S)\textbf{-mod}\rightleftharpoons\mathrm{QCoh}(T)\textbf{-mod}:\mathbf{res} $$

for the adjunction defined by extension and restriction of scalars along the map of symmetric monoidal categories

$$ f^{*}:\mathrm{QCoh}(S)\to\mathrm{QCoh}(T). $$

#### 2.1.2.

Let us recall some features of the theory of sheaves of categories.

To every prestack $\mathscr{Y}$ , one associates the symmetric monoidal $(\infty,2)$ -category

$$ \operatorname{ShCat}(\mathscr{Y})=\lim_{S\to\mathscr{Y}}\mathrm{QCoh}(S)\textbf{-mod} $$

of sheaves of categories on $\mathscr{Y}$ . This limit is taken over test affine schemes mapping to $\mathscr{Y}$ , with the transition functors given by $\mathbf{ind}$ . The value of a sheaf of categories $\mathscr{C}$ at a test affine scheme $S$ is denoted

$$ \mathbf{\Gamma}(S;\mathscr{C})\in\mathrm{QCoh}(S)\textbf{-mod}. $$

The monoidal unit of $\operatorname{ShCat}(\mathscr{Y})$ is denoted $\mathrm{QCoh}_{/\mathscr{Y}}$ . It is given by the assignment

$$ \mathbf{\Gamma}(S;\mathrm{QCoh}_{/\mathscr{Y}})=\mathrm{QCoh}(S). $$

To a morphism of prestacks $f:\mathscr{Z}\to\mathscr{Y}$ , one associates the adjunction

$$ \mathbf{cores}_{f}:\operatorname{ShCat}(\mathscr{Y})\rightleftharpoons\operatorname{ShCat}(\mathscr{Z}):\mathbf{coind}_{f}. $$

For any cartesian diagram of prestacks

$$ {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathscr{Z}^{\prime}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathscr{Z}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathscr{Y}^{\prime}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathscr{Y}} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces g^{\prime}} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f^{\prime}} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces g} $$

the natural transformation

$$ \mathbf{cores}_{g}\circ\mathbf{coind}_{f}\to\mathbf{coind}_{f^{\prime}}\circ\mathbf{cores}_{g^{\prime}} $$

obtained by adjunction from the identification

$$ \mathbf{cores}_{f^{\prime}}\circ\mathbf{cores}_{g}\overset{\sim}{\rightarrow}\mathbf{cores}_{g^{\prime}}\circ\mathbf{cores}_{f} $$

is an isomorphism.

#### 2.1.3.

Note that

$$ \mathbf{coind}_{f}(\mathrm{QCoh}_{/\mathscr{Z}}) $$

is naturally a sheaf of symmetric monoidal categories over $\operatorname{ShCat}(\mathscr{Y})$ , and the adjunction (2.1.1) enhances to an adjunction

$$ \mathbf{Loc}_{\mathscr{Z}/\mathscr{Y}}:\mathbf{coind}_{f}(\mathrm{QCoh}_{/\mathscr{Z}})\textbf{-mod}(\operatorname{ShCat}(\mathscr{Y}))\rightleftharpoons\operatorname{ShCat}(\mathscr{Z}):\mathbf{\Gamma}_{\mathscr{Z}/\mathscr{Y}} $$

The morphism $f$ is called relatively 1-affine when this adjunction is an equivalence.

#### 2.1.4.

A prestack $\mathscr{Y}$ is said to be 1-affine if the morphism $\mathscr{Y}\to\mathrm{pt}$ is relatively 1-affine. We remind the reader that:

- – Every (eventually coconnective, laft, with affine diagonal) algebraic stack is 1-affine.

- – The de Rham prestack $Z_{\mathrm{dR}}$ of any finite type scheme $Z$ is 1-affine.

### 2.2. Actions of sheared categories

#### 2.2.1.

Let ${\mathbf{G}_{m}}\textbf{-mod}$ denote the symmetric monoidal $(\infty,2)$ -category of dg categories with a weak action of ${\mathbf{G}_{m}}$ . Recall from [AG15, §A.2] that this category is equipped with a symmetric monoidal auto-equivalence, known as shearing:

$$ (-)^{\Rightarrow}:{\mathbf{G}_{m}}\textbf{-mod}\to{\mathbf{G}_{m}}\textbf{-mod}. $$

We write $(-)^{\Leftarrow}$ for its inverse.

#### 2.2.2.

Let $\mathscr{A}$ be a symmetric monoidal category acted on by ${\mathbf{G}_{m}}$ (that is, $\mathscr{A}$ is a commutative algebra object of ${\mathbf{G}_{m}}\textbf{-mod}$ ). Since shearing is symmetric monoidal, $\mathscr{A}^{\Rightarrow}$ is another symmetric monoidal category acted on by ${\mathbf{G}_{m}}$ .

The goal of this subsection is to give an answer to the question of what it takes equip a dg category $\mathscr{M}$ with an action of $\mathscr{A}^{\Rightarrow}$ (without regard for its ${\mathbf{G}_{m}}$ -action).

That is, we will give a description of

$$ \mathscr{A}^{\Rightarrow}\textbf{-mod}=\mathscr{A}^{\Rightarrow}\textbf{-mod}(\operatorname{dgCat}). $$

#### 2.2.3. A toy model

The construction we are about to give has an analogue one category level down. Namely, for a graded algebra $A$ , and a vector space $M$ , the following data are equivalent:

- (a) a non-graded $A$ -module structure on $M$ ;

- (b) a graded $A[t^{\pm 1}]$ -module structure on $M[t^{\pm 1}]$ .

Indeed, if $M$ is given a non-graded $A$ -module structure, then we endow $M[t^{\pm 1}]$ with the structure of a graded $A$ -module, where a homogeneous element $a$ of degree $n$ acts by

$$ a\cdot(mt^{k})=(am)t^{n+k}. $$

This action commutes with the natural graded action of $k[t^{\pm 1}]$ on $M[t^{\pm 1}]$ and hence makes $M[t^{\pm 1}]$ into a graded $A[t^{\pm 1}]$ -module. To recover the original non-graded action of $A$ of $M$ , observe that $A$ is the degree zero part of $A[t^{\pm 1}]$ and $M$ is the degree zero part of $M[t^{\pm 1}]$ .

#### 2.2.4.

Since the morphism $f:\mathrm{pt}\to B{\mathbf{G}_{m}}$ is relatively 1-affine, we obtain an identification

$$ \operatorname{dgCat}\simeq\mathrm{QCoh}({\mathbf{G}_{m}})\textbf{-mod}({\mathbf{G}_{m}}\textbf{-mod})\qquad\mathscr{M}\mapsto\mathscr{M}\otimes\mathrm{QCoh}({\mathbf{G}_{m}}) $$

where $\mathrm{QCoh}({\mathbf{G}_{m}})$ is viewed as a ${\mathbf{G}_{m}}$ -equivariant symmetric monoidal category via its pointwise tensor product.

Now let $\mathscr{B}$ be any symmetric monoidal category. From the monadic adjunction

$$ \mathbf{ind}:\operatorname{dgCat}\rightleftharpoons\mathscr{B}\textbf{-mod}(\operatorname{dgCat}):\mathbf{oblv}, $$

we obtain a commutative diagram

$$ {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathscr{B}\textbf{-mod}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\big(\mathscr{B}\otimes\mathrm{QCoh}({\mathbf{G}_{m}})\big)\textbf{-mod}({\mathbf{G}_{m}}\textbf{-mod})} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{dgCat}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{QCoh}({\mathbf{G}_{m}})\textbf{-mod}({\mathbf{G}_{m}}\textbf{-mod})} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{oblv}} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sim} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{oblv}} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sim} $$

in which both horizontal arrows are equivalences.

#### 2.2.5.

Now let $\mathscr{B}$ be the underlying symmetric monoidal category of $\mathscr{A}^{\Rightarrow}$ . By the projection formula for sheaves of categories we obtain the equivalences of commutative algebras

$$ \displaystyle\mathscr{B}\otimes\mathrm{QCoh}({\mathbf{G}_{m}}) \displaystyle\simeq\mathbf{coind}_{f}\circ\mathbf{cores}_{f}\left(\mathscr{A}^{\Rightarrow}\right) \displaystyle\qquad\simeq\mathscr{A}^{\Rightarrow}\otimes\mathbf{coind}_{f}(\mathrm{Vect})\simeq\mathscr{A}^{\Rightarrow}\otimes\mathrm{QCoh}({\mathbf{G}_{m}}) $$

in ${\mathbf{G}_{m}}\textbf{-mod}$ .

As a result, for our choice of $\mathscr{B}$ , the diagram (2.2.1) rewrites as

$$ {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathscr{A}^{\Rightarrow}\textbf{-mod}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\big(\mathscr{A}^{\Rightarrow}\otimes\mathrm{QCoh}({\mathbf{G}_{m}})\big)\textbf{-mod}({\mathbf{G}_{m}}\textbf{-mod})} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{dgCat}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{QCoh}({\mathbf{G}_{m}})\textbf{-mod}({\mathbf{G}_{m}}\textbf{-mod})} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{oblv}} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sim} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{oblv}} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sim} $$

The difference between this diagram and (2.2.1) is that here the ${\mathbf{G}_{m}}$ action on $\mathscr{A}^{\Rightarrow}\otimes\mathrm{QCoh}({\mathbf{G}_{m}})$ is the natural one coming from the preexisting action on $\mathscr{A}^{\Rightarrow}$ , while in (2.2.1) the ${\mathbf{G}_{m}}$ action on $\mathscr{B}$ is trivial.

#### 2.2.6.

Note that shearing induces a commutative diagram

$$ {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\big(\mathscr{A}^{\Rightarrow}\otimes\mathrm{QCoh}({\mathbf{G}_{m}})\big)\textbf{-mod}({\mathbf{G}_{m}}\textbf{-mod})} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\big(\mathscr{A}\otimes\mathrm{QCoh}({\mathbf{G}_{m}})^{\Leftarrow}\big)\textbf{-mod}({\mathbf{G}_{m}}\textbf{-mod})} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{QCoh}({\mathbf{G}_{m}})\textbf{-mod}({\mathbf{G}_{m}}\textbf{-mod})} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{QCoh}({\mathbf{G}_{m}})^{\Leftarrow}\textbf{-mod}({\mathbf{G}_{m}}\textbf{-mod})} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{oblv}} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces(-)^{\Leftarrow}} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{oblv}} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces(-)^{\Leftarrow}} $$

in which the horizontal arrows are equivalences. Concatenating this with (2.2.2), we obtain the commutative diagram

$$ {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathscr{A}^{\Rightarrow}\textbf{-mod}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\big(\mathscr{A}\otimes\mathrm{QCoh}({\mathbf{G}_{m}})^{\Leftarrow}\big)\textbf{-mod}({\mathbf{G}_{m}}\textbf{-mod})} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{dgCat}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{QCoh}({\mathbf{G}_{m}})^{\Leftarrow}\textbf{-mod}({\mathbf{G}_{m}}\textbf{-mod})} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{oblv}} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sim} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{oblv}} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sim} $$

where the lower horizontal equivalence is given by

$$ \mathscr{M}\mapsto\mathscr{M}\otimes\mathrm{QCoh}({\mathbf{G}_{m}})^{\Leftarrow}. $$

#### 2.2.7.

This is our answer to the question posed in §2.2.2: giving an action of $\mathscr{A}^{\Rightarrow}$ on $\mathscr{M}$ is equivalent to giving a ${\mathbf{G}_{m}}$ -equivariant action of $\mathscr{A}$ on

$$ \mathscr{M}\otimes\mathrm{QCoh}({\mathbf{G}_{m}})^{\Leftarrow}, $$

commuting with the natural ${\mathbf{G}_{m}}$ -equivariant action of $\mathrm{QCoh}({\mathbf{G}_{m}})^{\Leftarrow}$ on the right factor.

#### 2.2.8. Remark

Since

$$ \mathrm{QCoh}({\mathbf{G}_{m}})^{\Leftarrow}\simeq k[\beta^{\pm}]\operatorname{-mod} $$

where $|\beta|=2$ , the category $\mathscr{M}\otimes\mathrm{QCoh}({\mathbf{G}_{m}})^{\Leftarrow}$ is a 2-periodization of $\mathscr{M}$ . One may interpret the result of this subsection as a deperiodization statement, showing what additional data is needed to reconstruct an action of $\mathscr{A}^{\Rightarrow}$ on $\mathscr{M}$ from an action of $\mathscr{A}$ on the 2-periodization of $\mathscr{M}$ .

### 2.3. Geometric incarnation of shearing

#### 2.3.1.

For the rest this section, we will let $Z$ denote a fixed choice of quasi-smooth scheme. In light of §2.2, Construction 2.0.0 admits the following reformulation:

#### 2.3.1 Construction.

There is a natural lift of

$$ \mathrm{IndCoh}(Z)\otimes\mathrm{QCoh}({\mathbf{G}_{m}})^{\Leftarrow}\in\mathrm{QCoh}({\mathbf{G}_{m}})^{\Leftarrow}\textbf{-mod}({\mathbf{G}_{m}}\textbf{-mod}) $$

to an object of

$$ \big(\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(Z))\otimes\mathrm{QCoh}({\mathbf{G}_{m}})^{\Leftarrow}\big)\textbf{-mod}({\mathbf{G}_{m}}\textbf{-mod}). $$

#### 2.3.2.

Our next task is to reformulate Construction 2.3.1 by giving a geometric incarnation of $\mathrm{QCoh}({\mathbf{G}_{m}})^{\Leftarrow}$ , viewed as a symmetric monoidal category with its dilation action of ${\mathbf{G}_{m}}$ .

Regard $\mathrm{IndCoh}(\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1})$ as a symmetric monoidal category under convolution. Under the Koszul duality equivalence (1.3.1) for $V=\mathbf{A}^{1}$ , the monoidal localization

$$ (j^{*})^{\Rightarrow}:\mathrm{QCoh}(\mathbf{A}^{1})^{\Rightarrow}\to\mathrm{QCoh}({\mathbf{G}_{m}})^{\Rightarrow} $$

goes over the monoidal localization

$$ \mathrm{IndCoh}(\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1})\to\overset{\circ}{\mathrm{IndCoh}}(\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1}). $$

Therefore, we obtain an ${\mathbf{G}_{m}}$ -equivariant equivalence of symmetric monoidal categories

$$ \overset{\circ}{\mathrm{IndCoh}}(\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1})\simeq\mathrm{QCoh}({\mathbf{G}_{m}})^{\Rightarrow}, $$

intertwining the inverse dilation action on the LHS with the dilation action on the RHS. After inverting the ${\mathbf{G}_{m}}$ action on the RHS, we obtain a symmetric monoidal equivalence

$$ \overset{\circ}{\mathrm{IndCoh}}(\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1})\simeq\mathrm{QCoh}({\mathbf{G}_{m}})^{\Leftarrow} $$

which is equivariant for the dilation actions on both sides.

It follows that Construction 2.3.1 admits the following reformulation:

#### 2.3.2 Construction.

There is a natural lift of

$$ \mathrm{IndCoh}(Z)\otimes\overset{\circ}{\mathrm{IndCoh}}(\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1})\in\overset{\circ}{\mathrm{IndCoh}}(\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1})\textbf{-mod}({\mathbf{G}_{m}}\textbf{-mod}). $$

to an object of

$$ \left(\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(Z))\otimes\overset{\circ}{\mathrm{IndCoh}}(\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1})\right)\textbf{-mod}({\mathbf{G}_{m}}\textbf{-mod}). $$

#### 2.3.3.

We will carry out Construction 2.3.2 by studying the product

$$ Z\times\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1}, $$

equipped with the action of ${\mathbf{G}_{m}}$ by dilation on the second factor.

To start off, $\mathbf{P}\mathrm{Sing}(Z\times\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1})$ inherits a ${\mathbf{G}_{m}}$ action by the naturality of $\mathrm{Sing}(-)$ , and we claim that

$$ \overset{\circ}{\mathrm{IndCoh}}(Z\times\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1})\in{\mathbf{G}_{m}}\textbf{-mod} $$

naturally lifts to an object

$$ \overset{\circ}{\mathrm{IndCoh}}(Z\times\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1})\in\mathrm{D}(\mathbf{P}\mathrm{Sing}(Z\times\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1}))\textbf{-mod}({\mathbf{G}_{m}}\textbf{-mod}). $$

In other words, we are saying that

$$ \overset{\circ}{\mathrm{IndCoh}}((Z\times\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1})/{\mathbf{G}_{m}})\simeq\overset{\circ}{\mathrm{IndCoh}}(Z\times\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1})^{\mathbf{G}_{m}}\in\mathrm{Rep}({\mathbf{G}_{m}})\textbf{-mod} $$

admits a natural lift to

$$ \begin{split}&\operatorname{ShCat}(\mathbf{P}\mathrm{Sing}(Z\times\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1})_{\mathrm{dR}}/{\mathbf{G}_{m}})\\
&\qquad\qquad\simeq\mathrm{D}(\mathbf{P}\mathrm{Sing}(Z\times\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1}))^{\mathbf{G}_{m}}\textbf{-mod}(\mathrm{Rep}({\mathbf{G}_{m}})\textbf{-mod}).\end{split} $$

Indeed, applying [AG18, Proposition-Construction 1.5.2] to the quotient stack

$$ (Z\times\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1})/{\mathbf{G}_{m}} $$

produces a lift of (2.3.3) to a sheaf of categories over

$$ \mathbf{P}\mathrm{Sing}((Z\times\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1})/{\mathbf{G}_{m}})_{\mathrm{dR}}\underset{((Z\times\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1})/{\mathbf{G}_{m}})_{\mathrm{dR}}}{\times}(Z\times\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1})/{\mathbf{G}_{m}}, $$

and this last stack maps to

$$ \begin{split}&\mathbf{P}\mathrm{Sing}((Z\times\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1})/{\mathbf{G}_{m}})_{\mathrm{dR}}\underset{((Z\times\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1})/{\mathbf{G}_{m}})_{\mathrm{dR}}}{\times}(Z\times\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1})_{\mathrm{dR}}/{\mathbf{G}_{m}}\\
&\qquad\qquad\simeq\mathbf{P}\mathrm{Sing}(Z\times\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1})_{\mathrm{dR}}/{\mathbf{G}_{m}}.\end{split} $$

#### 2.3.4.

One has

$$ \mathrm{Sing}(Z\times\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1})_{\mathrm{dR}}\simeq(\mathrm{Sing}(Z)\oplus\mathbf{1})_{\mathrm{dR}}, $$

where the latter expression denotes the de Rham prestack of $\mathrm{Sing}(Z)\underset{Z}{\times}\mathbf{A}^{1}_{Z}$ .

In terms of this identification, the action of ${\mathbf{G}_{m}}$ on $\mathrm{Sing}(Z\times\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1})$ obtained from the dilation action of ${\mathbf{G}_{m}}$ on $\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1}$ by the naturality of the $\mathrm{Sing}(-)$ construction matches with inverse dilation on $\mathbf{A}^{1}_{Z}$ .

Therefore, the open embedding

$$ \mathrm{Sing}(Z)\hookrightarrow\mathbf{P}(\mathrm{Sing}(Z)\oplus\mathbf{1})\simeq\mathbf{P}\mathrm{Sing}(Z\times\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1})\qquad\xi\mapsto[\xi:1]. $$

intertwines the action of ${\mathbf{G}_{m}}$ on its source by dilation with the preceding action of ${\mathbf{G}_{m}}$ on its target, and restricting (2.3.2) along this map defines a lift of

$$ \begin{split}\mathrm{IndCoh}(Z)&\otimes\overset{\circ}{\mathrm{IndCoh}}(\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1})\\
&\qquad\simeq\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(Z))\underset{\mathrm{D}(\mathbf{P}(\mathrm{Sing}(Z)\oplus\mathbf{1}))}{\otimes}\overset{\circ}{\mathrm{IndCoh}}(Z\times\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1})\in{\mathbf{G}_{m}}\textbf{-mod}\end{split} $$

to an object

$$ \mathrm{IndCoh}(Z)\otimes\overset{\circ}{\mathrm{IndCoh}}(\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1})\in\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(Z))\textbf{-mod}({\mathbf{G}_{m}}\textbf{-mod}). $$

We claim:

#### 2.3.4 Proposition.

The ${\mathbf{G}_{m}}$ -equivariant action $\mathrm{D}(\mathbf{P}\mathrm{Sing}(Z))$ on

$$ \mathrm{IndCoh}(Z)\otimes\overset{\circ}{\mathrm{IndCoh}}(\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1})\in{\mathbf{G}_{m}}\textbf{-mod} $$

encoded by (2.3.5) commutes with the ${\mathbf{G}_{m}}$ -equivariant action of $\overset{\circ}{\mathrm{IndCoh}}(\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1})$ encoded by (2.3.1).

#### 2.3.5.

Observe that Construction 2.3.2 follows immediately from Proposition 2.3.4. However, it is not clear a priori that Proposition 2.3.4 is actually a proposition (as opposed to a construction). This will be shown in §2.4, and the proof of Proposition 2.3.4 will appear in §2.5.

### 2.4. Relative crystals of categories

#### 2.4.1.

In this subsection, we will prove a general assertion about relative crystals of categories. A consequence of this result will be that the commutativity of the two actions appearing in Proposition 2.3.4 is merely a property and not additional data.

#### 2.4.2.

Let $\mathscr{Z}\to\mathscr{Y}$ be a schematic morphism of prestacks, and write

$$ p:\mathscr{Z}_{\mathrm{dR}/\mathscr{Y}}=\mathscr{Y}_{\mathrm{dR}}\underset{\mathscr{Z}_{\mathrm{dR}}}{\times}\mathscr{Z}\to\mathscr{Y} $$

for its formal completion.

#### 2.4.2 Proposition.

The functor

$$ \mathbf{coind}_{p}:\operatorname{ShCat}(\mathscr{Z}_{\mathrm{dR}/\mathscr{Y}})\to\operatorname{ShCat}(\mathscr{Y}) $$

is locally fully faithful44 4 A functor of $(\infty,2)$ -categories is said to be locally fully faithful if it induces fully faithful functors on mapping categories..

#### 2.4.3. Proof

Note that it suffices to consider the case where $\mathscr{Y}$ is an affine scheme. Indeed, under the identifications

$$ \operatorname{ShCat}(\mathscr{Z}_{\mathrm{dR}/\mathscr{Y}})\simeq\lim_{S}\operatorname{ShCat}((\mathscr{Z}_{S})_{\mathrm{dR}/S})\qquad\operatorname{ShCat}(\mathscr{Y})=\lim_{S}\operatorname{ShCat}(S), $$

where the limits are taken over all test affine schemes mapping to $\mathscr{Y}$ , the functor $\mathbf{coind}_{p}$ is the one induced by the functors

$$ \mathbf{coind}_{p_{S}}:\operatorname{ShCat}((\mathscr{Z}_{S})_{\mathrm{dR}/S})\to\operatorname{ShCat}(S). $$

#### 2.4.4.

Therefore, we may replace $\mathscr{Z}\to\mathscr{Y}$ with a map of schemes $Z\to Y$ , with $Y$ affine. Then $Y$ and $Z_{\mathrm{dR}/Y}$ are both 1-affine, and the $(\mathbf{cores},\mathbf{coind})$ adjunction identifies with

$$ \mathbf{ind}:\mathrm{QCoh}(Y)\textbf{-mod}\rightleftharpoons\mathrm{QCoh}(Z_{\mathrm{dR}/Y})\textbf{-mod}:\mathbf{res}. $$

In order to show that $\mathbf{res}$ is locally fully faithful, it suffices to check that the counit

$$ \mathbf{ind}\circ\mathbf{res}(\mathscr{C})\to\mathscr{C} $$

is a colocalization; i.e. that it admits a fully faithful left adjoint.

The counit under consideration is given by the morphism of $\mathrm{QCoh}(Z_{\mathrm{dR}/Y})$ -bimodules

$$ \begin{split}&\mathrm{QCoh}(Z_{\mathrm{dR}/Y})\underset{\mathrm{QCoh}(Y)}{\otimes}\mathrm{QCoh}(Z_{\mathrm{dR}/Y})\\
&\hskip 80.00012pt\simeq\mathrm{QCoh}((Z\times_{Y}Z)_{\mathrm{dR}/Y})\overset{\Delta_{\mathrm{dR}/Y}^{*}}{\longrightarrow}\mathrm{QCoh}(Z_{\mathrm{dR}/Y}),\end{split} $$

so it suffices to show that $\Delta_{\mathrm{dR}/Y}^{*}$ admits a fully faithful $\mathrm{QCoh}(Z_{\mathrm{dR}/Y})$ -bilinear left adjoint.

By Kashiwara’s lemma, the functor

$$ \Delta_{\mathrm{dR}}^{*}:\mathrm{QCoh}((Z\times_{Y}Z)_{\mathrm{dR}})\to\mathrm{QCoh}(Z_{\mathrm{dR}}) $$

admits a fully faithful $\mathrm{QCoh}((Z\times_{Y}Z)_{\mathrm{dR}})$ -linear left adjoint. Tensoring up along

$$ -\underset{\mathrm{QCoh}(Y_{\mathrm{dR}})}{\otimes}\mathrm{QCoh}(Y) $$

shows that (2.4.1) admits a left adjoint with the desired properties.

∎[Proposition 2.4.2]

#### 2.4.5. Porism

Let us record some consequences of Proposition 2.4.2 (or, more precisely, its proof).

Let $\mathscr{C}$ be a sheaf of categories over $\mathscr{Z}_{\mathrm{dR}/\mathscr{Y}}$ . Then the data of $\mathscr{C}$ is encoded by the data of $\mathbf{coind}_{p}(\mathscr{C})$ along with compatible choices of colocalizing subcategories

$$ \mathscr{C}_{S}\hookrightarrow\mathrm{QCoh}(S)\otimes\mathbf{\Gamma}(\mathscr{Y};\mathbf{coind}_{p}(\mathscr{C})) $$

for every test affine scheme mapping to $\mathscr{Y}$ .

We note for future reference that the functor (2.4.2) and its right adjoint are $\mathrm{QCoh}(S)$ -linear.

Let $\mathscr{D}$ be another sheaf of categories over $\mathscr{Z}_{\mathrm{dR}/\mathscr{Y}}$ . Then a morphism $\mathscr{C}\to\mathscr{D}$ in $\operatorname{ShCat}(\mathscr{Z})$ amounts to a morphism

$$ F:\mathbf{coind}_{p}(\mathscr{C})\to\mathbf{coind}_{p}(\mathscr{D}) $$

in $\operatorname{ShCat}(\mathscr{Y})$ with the property: for every test affine scheme mapping to $\mathscr{Y}$ , the functor

$$ \begin{split}\mathbf{1}_{\mathrm{QCoh}(S)}\otimes\mathbf{\Gamma}(S;F):\mathrm{QCoh}(S)&\otimes\mathbf{\Gamma}(S;\mathbf{coind}_{p}(\mathscr{C}))\\
&\qquad\to\mathrm{QCoh}(S)\otimes\mathbf{\Gamma}(S;\mathbf{coind}_{p}(\mathscr{D}))\end{split} $$

takes $\mathscr{C}_{S}$ into $\mathscr{D}_{S}$ .

Let $\mathscr{A}$ be a sheaf of monoidal categories over $\mathscr{Y}$ . Then an action of $\mathbf{cores}_{p}(\mathscr{A})$ on $\mathscr{C}$ amounts to an action of $\mathscr{A}$ on $\mathbf{coind}_{p}(\mathscr{C})$ with the property: for every test affine scheme mapping to $\mathscr{Y}$ , the action map

$$ \begin{split}&\mathrm{QCoh}(S)\otimes\mathbf{\Gamma}(S;\mathbf{coind}_{p}(\mathscr{C}))\underset{\mathrm{QCoh}(S)}{\otimes}\mathbf{\Gamma}(S;\mathscr{A})\\
&\qquad\qquad\simeq\mathrm{QCoh}(S)\otimes\mathbf{\Gamma}\left(S;\mathbf{coind}_{p}(\mathscr{C})\underset{\mathscr{Y}}{\otimes}\mathscr{A}\right)\\
&\hskip 80.00012pt\overset{\mathbf{1}\otimes\mathbf{\Gamma}(S;\mathrm{act})}{\longrightarrow}\mathrm{QCoh}(S)\otimes\mathbf{\Gamma}(S;\mathbf{coind}_{p}(\mathscr{C}))\end{split} $$

restricts to a functor

$$ \mathscr{C}_{S}\underset{\mathrm{QCoh}(S)}{\otimes}\mathbf{\Gamma}(S;\mathscr{A})\to\mathscr{C}_{S}. $$

### 2.5. Proof of Proposition 2.3.4

#### 2.5.1.

We apply the paradigm of §2.4 in the case

$$ \mathscr{Z}=\mathrm{Sing}(Z)/{\mathbf{G}_{m}}\subset\mathbf{P}(\mathrm{Sing}(Z)\oplus\mathbf{1})/{\mathbf{G}_{m}}\qquad\mathscr{Y}=B{\mathbf{G}_{m}}. $$

We interpret (2.3.5) as making

into a sheaf of categories over $\mathscr{Z}_{\mathrm{dR}/\mathscr{Y}}$ , and (2.3.1) as encoding an action of

$$ \mathscr{A}^{\mathbf{G}_{m}}=\overset{\circ}{\mathrm{IndCoh}}(\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1})^{\mathbf{G}_{m}}, $$

viewed as a constant sheaf of symmetric monoidal categories on $\mathscr{Y}$ , on $\mathbf{coind}_{p}(\mathscr{C}^{\mathbf{G}_{m}})$ .

In these terms, the assertion of Proposition 2.3.4 says that the action of $\mathscr{A}^{\mathbf{G}_{m}}$ on $\mathbf{coind}_{p}(\mathscr{C}^{\mathbf{G}_{m}})$ lifts to an action of $\mathbf{cores}_{p}(\mathscr{A}^{\mathbf{G}_{m}})$ on $\mathscr{C}^{\mathbf{G}_{m}}$ . Therefore, it suffices to show: for every test affine scheme $T$ mapping to $\mathscr{Z}^{\prime}_{\mathrm{dR}}$ , the full subcategory

## 3. Compatibilities

#### 3.0.1.

We will show in Proposition 3.5.1 that the action of $\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(Z))^{\Rightarrow}$ on $\mathrm{IndCoh}(Z)$ constructed in §2 has the expected backwards compatibility with the action of $\mathrm{D}(\mathbf{P}\mathrm{Sing}(Z))$ on $\overset{\circ}{\mathrm{IndCoh}}(Z)$ constructed in [AG18]. When there is possibility for confusion, we will refer to the former as the inhomogeneous action and the latter as the homogeneous action.

The outline of this section is as follows:

- – In §3.1 we prove a few straightforward results about the action of $D(\mathrm{Sing}(Z))^{\Rightarrow}$ on $\mathrm{IndCoh}(Z)$ .

- – In §3.2 we record some results about the relation between $\mathrm{IndCoh}$ on formal schemes and the action of $D(\mathrm{Sing}(Z))^{\Rightarrow}$ . In particular we give a simple description of the category $\mathrm{IndCoh}_{0}(Y^{\wedge}_{Z})$ in terms of this action. The proofs of the results in this section are deferred to Subsections 3.3 and 3.4.

- – In §3.3 we show how to reduce the statements in §3.2 to Proposition 3.3.2, a statement about the Arinkin–Gaitsgory homogeneous action of $D(\mathbf{P}\mathrm{Sing}(Z))$ on the category of singularities, whose proof is deferred to §3.4.

- – In §3.4 we prove Proposition 3.3.2.

- – In §3.5 we prove a natural compatibility statement relating the inhomogeneous action and the homogeneous action. (Our proof of this compatibility takes Proposition 3.3.2 as input, which is why this subsection doesn’t appear earlier in this section.)

- – In §3.6 we give an alternative description of the inhomogeneous action when $Z$ is presented as a global complete intersection scheme. This version of the action was considered previously in [Ber20, Section 2.2], so this section gives a backwards compatibility between our construction and the construction of loc. cit.

### 3.1. The basics

#### 3.1.1.

In this subsection we will collect some features of the inhomogenous action which are more or less immediate from its construction.

#### 3.1.1 Proposition.

Let $\pi:\mathrm{Sing}(Z)\to Z$ denote the canonical projection. The restriction of the inhomogeneous action along the symmetric monoidal functor

$$ (\pi^{!})^{\Rightarrow}:\mathrm{D}(Z)\to\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(Z))^{\Rightarrow} $$

recovers the usual action of $\mathrm{D}(Z)$ on $\mathrm{IndCoh}(Z)$ .

#### 3.1.2. Proof

This follows from [AG18, Corollary 1.4.5(b)].

#### 3.1.3.

Now consider the zero section $Z\to\mathrm{Sing}(Z)$ and view $\mathrm{D}(Z)$ as tensored over $\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(Z))$ using this map. We claim:

#### 3.1.3 Proposition.

The full subcategory

$$ \mathrm{D}(Z)\underset{\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(Z))^{\Rightarrow}}{\otimes}\mathrm{IndCoh}(Z)\subset\mathrm{IndCoh}(Z) $$

is equal to

$$ \mathrm{QCoh}(Z)\subset\mathrm{IndCoh}(Z). $$

#### 3.1.4. Proof

Recall the action of $\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(Z))$ on

$$ \mathrm{IndCoh}(Z)\otimes\overset{\circ}{\mathrm{IndCoh}}(\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1}) $$

from (2.3.5). We need to show that the full subcategory

$$ \begin{split}\mathrm{D}(Z)\underset{\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(Z))}{\otimes}&\left(\mathrm{IndCoh}(Z)\otimes\overset{\circ}{\mathrm{IndCoh}}(\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1})\right)\\
&\qquad\subset\mathrm{IndCoh}(Z)\otimes\overset{\circ}{\mathrm{IndCoh}}(\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1})\end{split} $$

is equal to

$$ \mathrm{QCoh}(Z)\otimes\overset{\circ}{\mathrm{IndCoh}}(\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1})\subset\mathrm{IndCoh}(Z)\otimes\overset{\circ}{\mathrm{IndCoh}}(\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1}). $$

This is a consequence of the following assertion, Proposition 3.1.4.

∎[Proposition 3.1.3]

#### 3.1.4 Proposition.

Let $Z_{1}$ and $Z_{2}$ be schemes, and consider the closed embedding

$$ \mathbf{P}\mathrm{Sing}(Z_{1})\times Z_{2}\hookrightarrow\mathbf{P}\mathrm{Sing}(Z_{1}\times Z_{2})\qquad\xi\mapsto[\xi:0]. $$

Then

$$ \begin{split}&\mathrm{D}(\mathbf{P}\mathrm{Sing}(Z_{1})\times Z_{2})\underset{\mathrm{D}(\mathbf{P}\mathrm{Sing}(Z_{1}\times Z_{2}))}{\otimes}\overset{\circ}{\mathrm{IndCoh}}(Z_{1}\times Z_{2})\\
&\hskip 160.00024pt\simeq\overset{\circ}{\mathrm{IndCoh}}(Z_{1})\otimes\mathrm{QCoh}(Z_{2})\end{split} $$

as full subcategories of

$$ \overset{\circ}{\mathrm{IndCoh}}(Z_{1}\times Z_{2}). $$

#### 3.1.5. Proof

This follows from [AG18, Theorem-Construction 1.4.2(a)] and [AG15, Lemma 4.6.4].

∎[Proposition 3.1.4]

### 3.2. Relative D-modules

#### 3.2.1.

Let $f:Z\to Y$ be a morphism of quasi-smooth schemes. We will be interested in the category

$$ \mathrm{IndCoh}(Y^{\wedge}_{Z}). $$

By [AG18, Proposition 3.1.2], the functor of IndCoh $!$ -pullback

$$ f^{!}:\mathrm{IndCoh}(Y)\to\mathrm{IndCoh}(Y^{\wedge}_{Z}) $$

## 4. Morita equivalence

In this section we shall formulate and prove the second main result of our paper, Theorem 4.1.5, which says that $\mathrm{IndCoh}(Z)$ defines a Morita equivalence between $\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(Z))^{\Rightarrow}$ and the monoidal category $\mathbf{H}(Z)$ .

We then study the interaction of this equivalence with a morphism of quasi-smooth schemes $Z\to Y$ .

The outline of this section is as follows:

- – In §4.1 we describe how the action of $D(\mathrm{Sing}(Z))^{\Rightarrow}$ on $\mathrm{IndCoh}(Z)$ behaves under duality, and as a consequence we show that $\mathrm{IndCoh}(Z)$ upgrades to a $(D(\mathrm{Sing}(Z))^{\Rightarrow},\mathbf{H}(Z))$ -bimodule.

- – In §4.2 we give a new proof of a theorem of D. Ben-Zvi, S. Gunningham, and H. Orem on Morita bimodules. Their result [BZGO20, Theorem 1.3] appears as our Proposition 4.2.3 and Corollary 4.2.4.

- – In §4.3 we show that in our situation the hypotheses of Proposition 4.2.3 are satisfied.

- – In §4.4 we show that the additional hypothesis of Corollary 4.2.4 is satisfied, proving Theorem 4.1.5.

- – In §4.5 we calculate the image of the transfer bimodule $\mathbf{H}_{Z\to Y}$ under our Morita equivalence. (Recall from [Ber19] that $\mathbf{H}_{Z\to Y}$ characterizes the functoriality of the category $\mathbf{H}(Z)$ as $Z$ varies.)

- – In §4.6 we calculate the image of the composition map

$$ \mathbf{H}_{Z\leftarrow Y}\underset{\mathbf{H}(Y)}{\otimes}\mathbf{H}_{Y\leftarrow X}\to\mathbf{H}_{Z\leftarrow X} $$

under our Morita equivalence.

### 4.1. Bimodule structure on the category of ind-coherent sheaves

#### 4.1.1.

Let $\mathscr{M}$ be a module over

$$ \mathscr{A}=\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(Z))^{\Rightarrow}, $$

and suppose that $\mathscr{M}$ admits a dual $\mathscr{M}^{\vee}$ as a plain dg category. By [Che23, §A.3.9]88 8 Strictly speaking, loc. cit. only considers categories of the form $D(Z)$ , without shearing. However, the proof in loc. cit. only relies on the category-theoretic properties of $D(Z)$ as an object of $\operatorname{dgCat}$ . Since shearing is a symmetric-monoidal automorphism of ${\mathbf{G}_{m}}\textbf{-mod}$ the assumptions listed in loc. cit. are also satisfied in our situation., the composite

$$ \mathrm{Vect}\to\mathscr{M}\otimes\mathscr{M}^{\vee}\to\mathscr{M}\otimes_{\mathscr{A}}\mathscr{M}^{\vee} $$

forms the unit of an $\mathscr{A}$ -module duality.

The counit of the duality

## 5. Extension to stacks

In this section, we will establish an version of the Morita equivalence of Theorem 4.1.5 when the quasi-smooth scheme $Z$ is replaced with a quasi-smooth stack $\mathscr{Y}$ .

Let us point out that although we do have a natural bimodule structure

$$ \mathrm{IndCoh}(\mathscr{Y})\in(\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y}))^{\Rightarrow},\mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y}))\textbf{-bimod}, $$

the resulting functor

$$ \mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y})\textbf{-mod}\to\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y}))^{\Rightarrow}\textbf{-mod} $$

will usually not be an equivalence. This is essentially due to the failure of 1-affineness for the de Rham space of an algebraic stack. Because of this, the correct generalization of Theorem 4.1.5 to the setting of stacks will involve sheaves of $(\infty,2)$ -categories.

We will then return to the category $\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y}))^{\Rightarrow}\textbf{-mod}$ and its relation to $\mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y})$ and show that (5.0.1) is a colocalization in the $(\infty,2)$ -category 2-dgCat of stable $(\infty,2)$ -categories tensored over dgCat.

The outline of this section is as follows:

- – In §5.1 we describe a category $\operatorname{ShCat}_{{\mathbf{S}^{\Rightarrow}}}(\mathscr{Y})$ , associated to any quasi-smooth stack $\mathscr{Y}$ , which is related to $D(\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y}))^{\Rightarrow}\textbf{-mod}$ in the same way that crystals of categories are related to $D(\mathscr{Y})\textbf{-mod}$ .

- – In §5.2 we prove that $\operatorname{ShCat}_{{\mathbf{S}^{\Rightarrow}}}(\mathscr{Y})$ is equivalent to the category $\operatorname{ShCat}_{\mathbf{H}}(\mathscr{Y})$ defined in [Ber19]. This amounts to showing that our Morita equivalence Theorem 4.1.5 is sufficiently functorial as the scheme $Z$ varies.

- – In §5.3 we show that the result of §4.5 on the image of transfer bimodules under our Morita equivalence extends to stacks, conditional on a construction involving relative $D$ -modules Construction 5.3.1.

- – In §5.4 we carry out Construction 5.3.1.

- – In §5.5 we apply the results of the previous subsections to study the relationship between $D(\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y}))^{\Rightarrow}\textbf{-mod}$ and $\operatorname{ShCat}_{{\mathbf{S}^{\Rightarrow}}}(\mathscr{Y})$ .

#### 5.3.1.

On the other hand, from the morphism

$$ \mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y})_{\mathscr{Z}}\to\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y}), $$

The Morita equivalence (5.1.5) exchanges the objects

$$ \mathscr{D}\in\operatorname{ShCat}_{\mathbf{S}^{\Rightarrow}}(\mathscr{Y}) $$

So the challenge is to produce a morphism

$$ \underline{\mathrm{D}}(\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y})_{\mathscr{Z}})^{\Rightarrow}\to\mathscr{D} $$

in $\operatorname{ShCat}_{\mathbf{S}^{\Rightarrow}}(\mathscr{Y})$ . Once this has been done, it will be straightforward to verify that the value of (5.3.3) at every object of $\operatorname{Sm}_{/\mathscr{Y}}$ agrees with the equivalence (5.3.2), and hence that (5.3.3) itself is an equivalence.

We shall delay the execution of Construction 5.3.1 to §5.4, and use the remainder of this subsection to explain some of its consequences.

#### 5.3.3.

The colocalization

$$ \mathrm{IndCoh}_{0}(\mathscr{Y}^{\wedge}_{\mathscr{Z}})\rightleftharpoons\mathrm{IndCoh}(\mathscr{Y}^{\wedge}_{\mathscr{Z}}) $$

of $\mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y})$ -modules induces a colocalization

$$ \mathbf{Loc}(\mathrm{IndCoh}_{0}(\mathscr{Y}^{\wedge}_{\mathscr{Z}}))\rightleftharpoons\mathbf{Loc}(\mathrm{IndCoh}(\mathscr{Y}^{\wedge}_{\mathscr{Z}})). $$

On the other hand, observe that we may identify

$$ \mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Z}_{S}/S)\simeq S\underset{\mathscr{Y}}{\times}\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Z}/\mathscr{Y}) $$

as closed subschemes of (5.3.1). In particular, we obtain a colocalization

$$ \underline{\mathrm{D}}(\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Z}/\mathscr{Y}))^{\Rightarrow}\rightleftharpoons\underline{\mathrm{D}}(\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y})_{\mathscr{Z}})^{\Rightarrow} $$

in $\operatorname{ShCat}_{\mathbf{S}^{\Rightarrow}}(\mathscr{Y})$ whose value an object $S\in\operatorname{Sm}_{/\mathscr{Y}}$ is given by the colocalization

$$ \mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Z}_{S}/S))^{\Rightarrow}\rightleftharpoons\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(S)_{\mathscr{Z}_{S}})^{\Rightarrow}. $$

#### 5.3.3 Proposition.

Construction 5.3.1 exchanges the colocalizations

$$ \underline{\mathrm{D}}(\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Z}/\mathscr{Y}))^{\Rightarrow}\qquad\text{and}\qquad\mathbf{Loc}(\mathrm{IndCoh}_{0}(\mathscr{Y}^{\wedge}_{\mathscr{Z}})). $$

#### 5.3.4.

Under our running assumptions on stacks (see §1.5.3) for every schematic morphism $f:\mathscr{Z}\to\mathscr{Y}$ of quasi-smooth stacks the graph $\Gamma_{f}:\mathscr{Z}\to\mathscr{Z}\times\mathscr{Y}$ is also schematic. Recall that one may consider the $(\mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Z}),\mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y}))$ -bimodule

$$ \mathbf{H}_{\mathscr{Z}\to\mathscr{Y}}=\mathrm{IndCoh}_{0}((\mathscr{Z}\times\mathscr{Y})^{\wedge}_{\mathscr{Z}}). $$

Recall also the correspondence of stacks

$$ {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y})_{\mathscr{Z}}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Z})} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y})} $$

induced by the singular codifferential of $f$ . Let us form the object

$$ \underline{\mathrm{D}}(\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y})_{\mathscr{Z}})^{\Rightarrow}\in\operatorname{ShCat}_{\mathbf{S}^{\Rightarrow}}(\mathscr{Z}\times\mathscr{Y}) $$

obtained from the morphism

$$ \mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y})_{\mathscr{Z}}\overset{\text{(\ref{eqn:singular_codifferential_stack})}}{\longrightarrow}\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Z})\times\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y})\overset{\tau\times\mathbf{1}}{\longrightarrow}\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Z})\times\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y}). $$

Since (5.3.6) identifies with the map

$$ \mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Z}/\mathscr{Z}\times\mathscr{Y})\to\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Z}\times\mathscr{Y})_{\mathscr{Z}} $$

associated to the graph of $f$

$$ \mathscr{Z}\to\mathscr{Z}\times\mathscr{Y}, $$

we obtain the following consequence of Proposition 5.3.3:

#### 5.3.4 Construction.

The Morita equivalence (5.1.5) for $\mathscr{Z}\times\mathscr{Y}$ exchanges the objects

$$ \underline{\mathrm{D}}(\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y})_{\mathscr{Z}})^{\Rightarrow}\qquad\text{and}\qquad\mathbf{Loc}(\mathbf{H}_{\mathscr{Z}\to\mathscr{Y}}) $$

### 5.4. Execution of Construction 5.3.1

#### 5.4.1.

As indicated in §5.3.2, the task at hand is more or less to construct the morphism (5.3.3). This will be accomplished by subjecting the functor of IndCoh $!$ -pullback

$$ \mathrm{IndCoh}(\mathscr{Y})\to\mathrm{IndCoh}(\mathscr{Y}^{\wedge}_{\mathscr{Z}}), $$

viewed as a morphism of $\mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y})$ -modules, to a series of transformations.

First we apply $\mathbf{Loc}$ to (5.4.1), and obtain a morphism

$$ \mathbf{Loc}(\mathrm{IndCoh}(\mathscr{Y}))\to\mathbf{Loc}(\mathrm{IndCoh}(\mathscr{Y}^{\wedge}_{\mathscr{Z}})) $$

in $\operatorname{ShCat}_{\mathbf{H}}(\mathscr{Y})$ .

Then (5.4.2) may be viewed as a morphism

$$ \underline{\mathrm{D}}(\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y}))^{\Rightarrow}\to\mathscr{D} $$

in $\operatorname{ShCat}_{\mathbf{S}^{\Rightarrow}}(\mathscr{Y})$ .

#### 5.4.2. Digression

To proceed further, we will need to introduce the category

$$ \operatorname{ShCat}_{\mathbf{S}^{\Rightarrow}}(\mathscr{Y})_{\mathscr{Z}}=\lim_{S\to\mathscr{Y}}\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(S)_{\mathscr{Z}_{S}})^{\Rightarrow}\textbf{-mod}, $$

where the limit is taken over $(\operatorname{Sm}_{/\mathscr{Y}})^{\mathrm{op}}$ with respect to the transition functors of induction:

$$ \mathbf{ind}:\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(S)_{\mathscr{Z}_{S}})^{\Rightarrow}\textbf{-mod}\to\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(T)_{\mathscr{Z}_{T}})^{\Rightarrow}\textbf{-mod} $$

Consider the adjunctions

making the following diagrams commute:

#### 5.4.3.

Note that the value of (5.4.2) at an object $S\in\operatorname{Sm}_{/\mathscr{Y}}$ is given by the functor of IndCoh $!$ -pullback

$$ \mathrm{IndCoh}(S)\to\mathrm{IndCoh}(S^{\wedge}_{\mathscr{Z}_{S}}), $$

regarded as a morphism of $\mathbf{H}(S)$ -modules.

We may view (5.4.7) as the functor

$$ \mathrm{IndCoh}(S)\to\mathrm{IndCoh}(S)\underset{\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(S))^{\Rightarrow}}{\otimes}\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(S)_{\mathscr{Z}_{S}})^{\Rightarrow}, $$

induced by the D-module $!$ -pullback

$$ \mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(S))^{\Rightarrow}\to\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(S)_{\mathscr{Z}_{S}})^{\Rightarrow}. $$

In other words, the value (5.4.3) at $S$ identifies with the morphism (5.4.8).

In particular, this lifts $\mathscr{D}_{S}$ to an object

$$ \tilde{\mathscr{D}}_{S}\in\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(S)_{\mathscr{Z}_{S}})^{\Rightarrow}\textbf{-mod}. $$

We claim:

#### 5.4.3 Proposition.

The data of $\tilde{\mathscr{D}}_{S}$ for $S\in\operatorname{Sm}_{/\mathscr{Y}}$ determine a lift of $\mathscr{D}$ to an object

$$ \tilde{\mathscr{D}}\in\operatorname{ShCat}_{\mathbf{S}^{\Rightarrow}}(\mathscr{Y})_{\mathscr{Z}}. $$

#### 5.4.4.

Note that this assertion is a proposition and not a construction as Proposition 2.4.2 (which is applicable by the running assumption that $\mathscr{Z}\to\mathscr{Y}$ is schematic) implies that the functors $\mathbf{oblv}_{S}$ are locally fully faithful. Namely, it amounts to the assertion that for every arrow $T\to S$ in $\operatorname{Sm}_{/\mathscr{Y}}$ , the map of $\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(T))^{\Rightarrow}$ -modules

$$ \begin{split}\mathbf{oblv}_{T}\circ\mathbf{ind}_{T\to S}(\tilde{\mathscr{D}}_{S})\simeq\mathbf{ind}_{T\to S}\circ\mathbf{oblv}_{S}(\tilde{\mathscr{D}}_{S})&\simeq\mathbf{ind}_{T\to S}(\mathscr{D}_{S})\\
&\qquad\overset{\sim}{\rightarrow}\mathscr{D}_{T}\simeq\mathbf{oblv}_{T}(\tilde{\mathscr{D}}_{T})\end{split} $$

is actually linear over $\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(T)_{\mathscr{Z}_{T}})^{\Rightarrow}$ .

#### 5.4.5.

We now take Proposition 5.4.3 as given and resume the construction of (5.3.3). Its proof will appear at the end of this subsection, §5.4.7.

By Proposition 5.4.3, we may perceive (5.4.3) as a morphism

$$ \underline{\mathrm{D}}(\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y}))^{\Rightarrow}\to\mathbf{oblv}(\tilde{\mathscr{D}}) $$

in $\operatorname{ShCat}_{\mathbf{S}^{\Rightarrow}}(\mathscr{Y})$ .

The transpose of (5.4.10) under the $(\mathbf{ind},\mathbf{oblv})$ adjunction is a morphism

$$ \mathbf{ind}(\underline{\mathrm{D}}(\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y}))^{\Rightarrow})\to\tilde{\mathscr{D}} $$

in $\operatorname{ShCat}_{\mathbf{S}^{\Rightarrow}}(\mathscr{Y})_{\mathscr{Z}}$ .

After applying $\mathbf{oblv}$ to (5.4.11), we obtain a morphism

$$ \mathbf{oblv}\circ\mathbf{ind}(\underline{\mathrm{D}}(\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y}))^{\Rightarrow})\to\mathscr{D} $$

in $\operatorname{ShCat}_{\mathbf{S}^{\Rightarrow}}(\mathscr{Y})$ .

Finally, after making the identification (5.4.6), we find that (5.4.12) defines the sought-after morphism

$$ \underline{\mathrm{D}}(\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y})_{\mathscr{Z}})^{\Rightarrow}\to\mathscr{D} $$

in $\operatorname{ShCat}_{\mathbf{S}^{\Rightarrow}}(\mathscr{Y})$ .

#### 5.4.6.

To finish Construction 5.3.1, it remains to verify that (5.4.13) is an isomorphism. Indeed, by the description of (5.4.3) given in §5.4.3, the value of (5.4.13) at an object $S\in\operatorname{Sm}_{/\mathscr{Y}}$ is the canonical arrow

$$ \mathrm{D}(\mathscr{Z}_{S})\underset{\mathrm{D}(S)}{\otimes}\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(S))^{\Rightarrow}\overset{\sim}{\rightarrow}\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(S)_{\mathscr{Z}_{S}})^{\Rightarrow}. $$

∎[Construction 5.3.1]

Consider the diagram

### 5.5. Sheared crystals of categories on the stack of singularities

#### 5.5.1.

The goal of this somewhat digressive subsection is to study the relationship between $\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y}))^{\Rightarrow}\textbf{-mod}$ and $\operatorname{ShCat}_{\mathbf{S}^{\Rightarrow}}(\mathscr{Y})$ . We will see that they are connected by a pair of adjoint functors

$$ \mathbf{Loc}:\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y}))^{\Rightarrow}\textbf{-mod}\rightleftharpoons\operatorname{ShCat}_{\mathbf{S}^{\Rightarrow}}(\mathscr{Y}):\mathbf{\Gamma} $$

in 2-dgCat, and that this adjunction is in fact a colocalization. Applying the Morita equivalence (5.1.5) and the H-affineness equivalence, we obtain that $\mathrm{IndCoh}(\mathscr{Y})$ is naturally a $(\mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y}),\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y}))^{\Rightarrow})$ -bimodule defining a colocalization

$$ \mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y}))^{\Rightarrow}\hookrightarrow\mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y})\textbf{-mod}. $$

#### 5.5.2.

Observe that the family of functors

$$ \mathbf{ind}:\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y}))^{\Rightarrow}\textbf{-mod}\to\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(S))^{\Rightarrow}\textbf{-mod}. $$

assemble into a functor

$$ \mathbf{Loc}:\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y}))^{\Rightarrow}\textbf{-mod}\to\operatorname{ShCat}_{\mathbf{S}^{\Rightarrow}}(\mathscr{Y}). $$

We claim:

#### 5.5.2 Proposition.

The functor $\mathbf{Loc}$ admits a right adjoint in 2-dgCat.

#### 5.5.3.

It is easy to see that $\mathbf{Loc}$ admits a right adjoint

$$ \mathbf{\Gamma}:\operatorname{ShCat}_{\mathbf{S}^{\Rightarrow}}(\mathscr{Y})\to\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y}))^{\Rightarrow}\textbf{-mod}, $$

computed by the formula

$$ \mathscr{C}\mapsto\lim_{S\to\mathscr{Y}}\mathbf{\Gamma}(S;\mathscr{C}), $$

where the limit is taken over $\operatorname{Sm}_{/\mathscr{Y}}$ . The content of Proposition 5.5.2 is that this functor is continuous and commutes with the operation of tensoring with a plain dg category.

#### 5.5.4. Proof of Proposition 5.5.2

In light of the Morita equivalence (5.1.5) and the H-affineness theorem, it is equivalent to show that the functor

$$ \mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y}))^{\Rightarrow}\textbf{-mod}\overset{\mathbf{Loc}}{\longrightarrow}\operatorname{ShCat}_{\mathbf{S}^{\Rightarrow}}(\mathscr{Y})\overset{\sim}{\rightarrow}\operatorname{ShCat}_{\mathbf{H}}(\mathscr{Y})\overset{\sim}{\rightarrow}\mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y})\textbf{-mod} $$

admits a right adjoint in 2-dgCat.

Now observe that we have the adjunction

$$ \mathbf{ind}:\textbf{dgCat}\rightleftharpoons\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y}))^{\Rightarrow}\textbf{-mod}:\mathbf{oblv} $$

in 2-dgCat, where the right adjoint $\mathbf{oblv}$ is conservative. Therefore, it is enough to show that the composite

$$ \textbf{dgCat}\overset{\mathbf{ind}}{\longrightarrow}\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y}))^{\Rightarrow}\textbf{-mod}\to\mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y})\textbf{-mod} $$

admits a continuous right adjoint.

This functor is the one defined by $\mathrm{IndCoh}(\mathscr{Y})$ , as an $\mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y})$ -module. Therefore, it is equivalent to show that $\mathrm{IndCoh}(\mathscr{Y})$ is dualizable as an $\mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y})$ -module. This follows from the fact that $\mathrm{IndCoh}(\mathscr{Y})$ is dualizable as a plain dg category and that $\mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y})$ is rigid.

∎[Proposition 5.5.2]

#### 5.5.4 Proposition.

The functor $\mathbf{Loc}$ is fully faithful.

#### 5.5.5. Proof

Since $(\mathbf{Loc},\mathbf{\Gamma})$ is an adjunction in 2-dgCat, it suffices to check that the functor

$$ \mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y}))^{\Rightarrow}\to\operatorname{End}_{\operatorname{ShCat}_{\mathbf{S}^{\Rightarrow}}(\mathscr{Y})}\big(\mathbf{Loc}(\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y}))^{\Rightarrow})\big) $$

is an equivalence. But this functor rewrites as

$$ \mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y}))^{\Rightarrow}\to\lim_{S\to\mathscr{Y}}\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(S))^{\Rightarrow}, $$

where the limit is taken over $\operatorname{Sm}_{/\mathscr{Y}}$ , so the result follows from smooth descent for D-modules.

∎[Proposition 5.5.4]

#### 5.5.6. Remark

Note that we have a commutative diagram

$$ {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{D}(\mathscr{Y})\textbf{-mod}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{ShCat}(\mathscr{Y}_{\mathrm{dR}})} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y}))^{\Rightarrow}\textbf{-mod}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{ShCat}_{\mathbf{S}^{\Rightarrow}}(\mathscr{Y})} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{res}} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{Loc}} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{Loc}} $$

in which the vertical arrows are fully faithful. Therefore, Proposition 5.5.4 confirms [Gai15, Conjecture 2.6.6] for stacks which are nil-isomorphic to a quasi-smooth stack.

## 6. Trace computations

The outline of this section is as follows:

- – In §6.1 we review the basic formalism of categorical traces and prove some simple results about the behavior of traces with respect to duality. The results of this section are a categorification of the fact that the trace of a matrix equals the trace of its transpose.

- – In §6.2 we use Theorem 4.1.5 to calculate the trace of $\mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y})\textbf{-mod}$ with respect to the bimodule $\mathbf{H}_{\phi:\mathscr{Y}\to\mathscr{Y}}$ for any schematic endomorphism of a quasi-smooth stack.

- – In §6.3 we relate the Chern class of $\mathrm{IndCoh}(\mathscr{Y})$ as a “Weil-object” of $\mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y})\textbf{-mod}$ with the enhanced trace of [GKRV22].

- – In §6.4 we calculate how taking traces interacts with the singular support filtration on $\mathrm{IndCoh}(\mathscr{Y})$ .

### 6.1. Review of categorical trace

#### 6.1.1.

Recall that for any endomorphism $\phi:\mathscr{C}\to\mathscr{C}$ of a dualizable object in an ambient symmetric monoidal category $\mathbf{O}$ , it makes sense to form the trace

$$ \operatorname{tr}(\phi;\mathscr{C})\in\operatorname{End}(\mathbf{1}_{\mathbf{O}}), $$

given definitionally by the composite

$$ \mathbf{1}_{\mathbf{O}}\overset{\mathrm{coev}}{\longrightarrow}\mathscr{C}\otimes\mathscr{C}^{\vee}\overset{\phi\otimes\mathbf{1}}{\longrightarrow}\mathscr{C}\otimes\mathscr{C}^{\vee}\overset{\mathrm{ev}}{\longrightarrow}\mathbf{1}_{\mathbf{O}}. $$

Under the identification $\mathbf{1}_{\mathbf{O}}\simeq\mathbf{1}_{\mathbf{O}}^{\vee}$ the following diagram always naturally commutes

$$ {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{1}_{\mathbf{O}}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{1}_{\mathbf{O}}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{1}_{\mathbf{O}}^{\vee}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{1}_{\mathbf{O}}^{\vee}} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\psi} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sim} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sim} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\psi^{\vee}} $$

$$ \operatorname{tr}(\phi;\mathscr{C})\simeq\operatorname{tr}(\phi^{\vee};\mathscr{C}^{\vee}). $$

#### 6.1.4.

The $2$ -categorical functoriality of traces enjoys a further compatibility with duality. Namely, consider the natural transformation

$$ \alpha^{\vee}:\phi^{\vee}\circ F^{\vee}\to F^{\vee}\circ\phi^{\vee} $$

obtained from $\alpha$ by passing to dual functors. Since $F$ is right adjointable, $F^{\vee}$ is left adjointable with $(F^{\vee})^{L}\simeq(F^{R})^{\vee}$ . Therefore, we obtain from $\alpha^{\vee}$ a natural transformation

$$ \beta:(F^{\vee})^{L}\circ\phi^{\vee}\to\phi^{\vee}\circ(F^{\vee})^{L}. $$

We will obtain the following compatibility by a routine diagram chase:

#### 6.1.4 Computation.

There is a commutative diagram:

$$ {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{tr}(\phi;\mathscr{C})} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{tr}(\phi;\mathscr{D})} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{tr}(\phi^{\vee};\mathscr{C}^{\vee})} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{tr}(\phi^{\vee};\mathscr{D}^{\vee})} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{cl}(F,\alpha)} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sim} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sim} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{cl}((F^{\vee})^{L},\beta)} $$

#### 6.1.5.

Applying (6.1.2) to every arrow appearing in the definition of $\mathrm{cl}((F^{\vee})^{L},\beta)$ identifies the lower circuit of this diagram with the composite

$$ \begin{split}&\operatorname{tr}(\phi;\mathscr{C})\overset{\mathrm{unit}}{\longrightarrow}\operatorname{tr}(F^{R}\circ F\circ\phi;\mathscr{C})\simeq\operatorname{tr}(F\circ\phi\circ F^{R};\mathscr{D})\\
&\qquad\qquad\overset{\beta^{\vee}}{\longrightarrow}\operatorname{tr}(F\circ F^{R}\circ\phi;\mathscr{D})\overset{\mathrm{counit}}{\longrightarrow}\operatorname{tr}(\phi;\mathscr{D})\simeq\operatorname{tr}(\phi^{\vee};\mathscr{D}^{\vee}),\end{split} $$

where the second arrow is induced by the natural transformation

$$ \beta^{\vee}:\phi\circ F^{R}\to F^{R}\circ\phi. $$

Using the cyclic property of the trace, we rewrite the first line of (6.1.5) to replace it with

$$ \begin{split}&\operatorname{tr}(\phi;\mathscr{C})\overset{\mathrm{unit}}{\longrightarrow}\operatorname{tr}(\phi\circ F^{R}\circ F;\mathscr{C})\simeq\operatorname{tr}(F\circ\phi\circ F^{R};\mathscr{D})\\

$$ {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F\circ\phi\circ F^{R}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F\circ F^{R}\circ\phi} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\phi\circ F\circ F^{R}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\phi} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\beta^{\vee}} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{counit}} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{counit}} $$

#### 6.1.6.

Let $\mathscr{A}$ be a monoidal category and let $\Phi$ be an $(\mathscr{A},\mathscr{A})$ -bimodule, perceived as an endofunctor

$$ \Phi:\mathscr{A}\textbf{-mod}\to\mathscr{A}\textbf{-mod}\qquad\mathscr{M}\mapsto\Phi\otimes_{\mathscr{A}}\mathscr{M}. $$

It makes sense to take the trace of this endofunctor when $\Phi$ is right dualizable; this is the dg category

$$ \operatorname{tr}(\Phi;\mathscr{A}\textbf{-mod})=\mathscr{A}\underset{\mathscr{A}\otimes\mathscr{A}^{\mathrm{rev}}}{\otimes}\Phi. $$

Now let $(\mathscr{M},\alpha)$ be an $\mathscr{A}$ -module equipped with lax equivariance data for $\Phi$ ; that is, $\mathscr{M}$ is an $\mathscr{A}$ -module and $\alpha$ is a morphism of $\mathscr{A}$ -modules

$$ \alpha:\mathscr{M}\to\Phi\otimes_{\mathscr{A}}\mathscr{M}. $$

If $\mathscr{M}$ admits a right dual as an $\mathscr{A}$ -module, then one may form the Chern class

$$ \mathrm{cl}(\mathscr{M},\alpha)\in\operatorname{tr}(\Phi;\mathscr{A}\textbf{-mod}), $$

given by the composite

$$ \begin{split}\mathbf{1}\overset{\mathrm{coev}}{\longrightarrow}\mathscr{M}^{\vee}\otimes_{\mathscr{A}}\mathscr{M}&\overset{\mathbf{1}\otimes\alpha}{\longrightarrow}\mathscr{M}^{\vee}\otimes_{\mathscr{A}}(\Phi\otimes_{\mathscr{A}}\mathscr{M})\\
&\qquad\qquad\simeq(\mathscr{M}\otimes\mathscr{M}^{\vee})\underset{\mathscr{A}\otimes\mathscr{A}^{\mathrm{rev}}}{\otimes}\Phi\overset{\mathrm{ev}\otimes\mathbf{1}}{\longrightarrow}\mathscr{A}\underset{\mathscr{A}\otimes\mathscr{A}^{\mathrm{rev}}}{\otimes}\Phi.\end{split} $$

Let us note for future reference that this composite admits an alternative description. Since $\mathscr{M}$ is dualizable, we may view $\alpha$ as a morphism of $(\mathscr{A},\mathscr{A})$ -bimodules

$$ \alpha^{\prime}:\mathscr{M}\otimes\mathscr{M}^{\vee}\to\Phi. $$

Then (6.1.9) identifies with the composite

$$ \begin{split}\mathbf{1}&\overset{\mathrm{coev}}{\longrightarrow}\mathscr{M}^{\vee}\otimes_{\mathscr{A}}\mathscr{M}\\
&\qquad\qquad\simeq\mathscr{A}\underset{\mathscr{A}\otimes\mathscr{A}^{\mathrm{rev}}}{\otimes}(\mathscr{M}\otimes\mathscr{M}^{\vee})\to\mathscr{A}\underset{\mathscr{A}\otimes\mathscr{A}^{\mathrm{rev}}}{\otimes}\Phi.\end{split} $$

### 6.2. Carré du champ

#### 6.2.1.

Let $\phi:\mathscr{Y}\to\mathscr{Y}$ be a schematic endomorphism of a quasi-smooth stack. Consider the $(\mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y}),\mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y}))$ -bimodule

$$ \mathbf{H}_{\phi}=\mathbf{H}_{\mathscr{Y}\to\mathscr{Y}} $$

associated to the morphism $\phi$ by §5.3.4. We will use the same symbol to denote the corresponding endomorphism:

$$ \mathbf{H}_{\phi}:\mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y})\textbf{-mod}\to\mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y})\textbf{-mod}. $$

Observe that $\mathrm{IndCoh}(\mathscr{Y})$ is naturally equipped with a lax equivariance datum

$$ \alpha:\mathrm{IndCoh}(\mathscr{Y})\to\mathbf{H}_{\phi}\underset{\mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y})}{\otimes}\mathrm{IndCoh}(\mathscr{Y}) $$

for $\mathbf{H}_{\phi}$ , corresponding under the self-duality of $\mathrm{IndCoh}(\mathscr{Y})$ as an $\mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y})$ -module to the composite

$$ \mathrm{IndCoh}(\mathscr{Y}\times\mathscr{Y})\to\mathrm{IndCoh}((\mathscr{Y}\times\mathscr{Y})^{\wedge}_{\mathscr{Y}})\to\mathbf{H}_{\phi} $$

of IndCoh $!$ -pullback along the formal completion of graph of $\phi$ with the right adjoint of the colocalization defining $\mathbf{H}_{\phi}$ . The goal of this subsection is to give a description of the object

$$ \mathrm{cl}(\mathrm{IndCoh}(\mathscr{Y}),\alpha)\in\operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{H}_{\phi};\mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y})\textbf{-mod}). $$

#### 6.2.2.

Recall that a stack $\mathscr{X}$ is said to be quasi-quasi-smooth if its cotangent complex has tor amplitude $[2,-1]$ . When this happens, $\mathbf{L}_{\mathscr{X}}[-2]$ is a perfect complex of tor amplitude $[0,-3]$ and we may form the algebraic stack

$$ \mathrm{Sing}_{2}(\mathscr{X})=\operatorname{Spec}_{\mathscr{X}}\left(\mathrm{Sym}(\mathbf{L}_{\mathscr{X}}[-2])^{\vee}\right). $$

We think of $\mathrm{Sing}_{2}(\mathscr{X})$ as measuring the extent to which $\mathscr{X}$ fails to be quasi-smooth.

#### 6.2.3.

The reason we need to consider quasi-quasi-smooth stacks is that the stack of fixed points $\mathscr{Y}^{\phi}$ is not usually quasi-smooth. Instead, it is quasi-quasi-smooth, being a fiber product of quasi-smooth stacks:

$$ {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathscr{Y}^{\phi}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathscr{Y}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathscr{Y}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathscr{Y}\times\mathscr{Y}} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{1}\times\phi} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Delta} $$

One has that

$$ \mathrm{Sing}_{2}(\mathscr{Y}^{\phi})\simeq\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y}/\mathscr{Y}\times\mathscr{Y})\underset{\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y}\times\mathscr{Y})}{\times}\mathrm{Sing}_{\phi}(\mathscr{Y}/\mathscr{Y}\times\mathscr{Y}), $$

where

$$ \mathrm{Sing}_{\phi}(\mathscr{Y}/\mathscr{Y}\times\mathscr{Y})\to\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y})\times\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y}). $$

is the map (5.3.7) for the morphism $\phi$ .

#### 6.2.3 Computation.

We have

$$ \operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{H}_{\phi}(\mathscr{Y});\mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y})\textbf{-mod})\simeq\mathrm{D}\left(\mathrm{Sing}_{2}(\mathscr{Y}^{\phi})\right)^{\Rightarrow}, $$

and this identification takes the object

$$ \mathrm{cl}(\mathrm{IndCoh}(\mathscr{Y}),\alpha)\in\operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{H}_{\phi};\mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y})\textbf{-mod}) $$

to the object

$$ (\omega_{\mathrm{Sing}_{2}(\mathscr{Y}^{\phi})})^{\Rightarrow}\in\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}_{2}(\mathscr{Y}^{\phi}))^{\Rightarrow}. $$

#### 6.2.4.

Let us begin with the identification

$$ \begin{split}\operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{H}_{\phi};\mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y})\textbf{-mod})&\simeq\mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y})\underset{\mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y})\otimes\mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y})^{\mathrm{rev}}}{\otimes}\mathbf{H}_{\phi}\\
&\qquad\qquad\simeq\mathrm{Maps}_{(\mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y}),\mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y}))}(\mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y}),\mathbf{H}_{\phi}).\end{split} $$

Since the coevaluation

$$ \mathrm{Vect}\to\mathrm{IndCoh}(\mathscr{Y})\underset{\mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y})}{\otimes}\mathrm{IndCoh}(\mathscr{Y})\simeq\mathrm{Maps}_{(\mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y}),\mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y}))}(\mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y}),\mathrm{IndCoh}(\mathscr{Y}\times\mathscr{Y})) $$

classifies the map of $(\mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y}),\mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y}))$ -bimodules

$$ \mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y})\hookrightarrow\mathrm{IndCoh}((\mathscr{Y}\times\mathscr{Y})^{\wedge}_{\mathscr{Y}})\overset{(-)_{*}}{\longrightarrow}\mathrm{IndCoh}(\mathscr{Y}\times\mathscr{Y}), $$

the description (6.1.10) of Chern classes implies that the isomorphism (6.2.4) takes the class of $\mathrm{IndCoh}$ (6.2.3) to the object of

$$ \mathrm{Maps}_{(\mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y}),\mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y}))}(\mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y}),\mathbf{H}_{\phi}) $$

given by the composite

$$ \mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y})\to\mathrm{IndCoh}(\mathscr{Y}\times\mathscr{Y})\to\mathbf{H}_{\phi}. $$

After applying the equivalence

$$ (\mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y}),\mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y}))\textbf{-bimod}\simeq\mathbf{H}(\mathscr{Y}\times\mathscr{Y})\textbf{-mod}\simeq\operatorname{ShCat}_{\mathbf{H}}(\mathscr{Y}\times\mathscr{Y})\overset{\text{(\ref{eqn:morita_ShCat})}}{\longrightarrow}\operatorname{ShCat}_{\mathbf{S}^{\Rightarrow}}(\mathscr{Y}\times\mathscr{Y}), $$

we find that (6.2.4) identifies with

$$ \mathrm{Maps}_{\operatorname{ShCat}_{\mathbf{S}^{\Rightarrow}}(\mathscr{Y}\times\mathscr{Y})}\left(\underline{\mathrm{D}}(\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y}/\mathscr{Y}\times\mathscr{Y}))^{\Rightarrow},\underline{\mathrm{D}}(\mathrm{Sing}_{\phi}(\mathscr{Y}/\mathscr{Y}\times\mathscr{Y}))^{\Rightarrow}\right). $$

By §5.4.8, this identification sends (6.2.5) to the composite

$$ \underline{\mathrm{D}}(\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y}/\mathscr{Y}\times\mathscr{Y}))^{\Rightarrow}\to\underline{\mathrm{D}}(\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y}\times\mathscr{Y}))^{\Rightarrow}\to\underline{\mathrm{D}}(\mathrm{Sing}_{\phi}(\mathscr{Y}/\mathscr{Y}\times\mathscr{Y}))^{\Rightarrow} $$

in $\operatorname{ShCat}_{\mathbf{S}^{\Rightarrow}}(\mathscr{Y}\times\mathscr{Y})$ .

We finish the computation by writing (6.2.6) as the limit of the categories

$$ \begin{split}&\lim_{S\to\mathscr{Y}\times\mathscr{Y}}\mathrm{Maps}_{\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(S))^{\Rightarrow}}\left(\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y}/\mathscr{Y}\times\mathscr{Y})_{S})^{\Rightarrow},\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}_{\phi}(\mathscr{Y}/\mathscr{Y}\times\mathscr{Y})_{S})^{\Rightarrow}\right)\\
&\qquad\qquad\simeq\lim_{S\to\mathscr{Y}\times\mathscr{Y}}\mathrm{D}\left(\mathrm{Sing}_{2}(\mathscr{Y}^{\phi})_{S}\right)^{\Rightarrow}\simeq\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{Sing}_{2}(\mathscr{Y}^{\phi}))^{\Rightarrow}\end{split} $$

taken over $\operatorname{Sm}_{/\mathscr{Y}\times\mathscr{Y}}$ . By base-change for the Cartesian diagram

$$ {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{Sing}_{2}(\mathscr{Y}^{\phi})} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y}/\mathscr{Y}\times\mathscr{Y})} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{Sing}_{\phi}(\mathscr{Y}/\mathscr{Y}\times\mathscr{Y})} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{Sing}(\mathscr{Y}\times\mathscr{Y})} $$

the composite arrow (6.2.7) is sent to $(\omega_{\mathrm{Sing}_{2}(\mathscr{Y}^{\phi})})^{\Rightarrow}$ under (6.2.8).

## Appendix A Locally fully faithful functors

In this appendix we will formulate and prove a lifting criterion Proposition A.2.2 for locally fully faithful functors.

#### A.0.1.

Recall that a functor of $(\infty,2)$ -categories

$$ F:\mathscr{C}\to\mathscr{D} $$

is said to be locally fully faithful if, for every pair of objects $c,c^{\prime}\in\mathscr{C}$ , the functor

$$ \mathrm{Maps}_{\mathscr{C}}(c,c^{\prime})\to\mathrm{Maps}_{\mathscr{D}}(F(c),F(c^{\prime})) $$

is fully faithful.

Let us say right away that Proposition A.2.2 is concerned with functors out of an $(\infty,1)$ -category. Since the condition of being locally fully faithful is preserved by passage to $(\infty,1)$ -cores, the ambit of this appendix is contained entirely in the world of $(\infty,1)$ -categories.

#### A.0.2.

Recall that for any category $\mathscr{C}$ , one associates its twisted arrows category $\operatorname{Tw}(\mathscr{C})$ , whose objects are arrows $c\to c^{\prime}$ in $\mathscr{C}$ and whose morphisms from $c\to c^{\prime}$ to $d\to d^{\prime}$ are1313 13 Warning: the literature does not appear to be consistent as to whether the ‘twisted arrows category’ is what we have denoted $\operatorname{Tw}(\mathscr{C})$ or rather its opposite $\operatorname{Tw}(\mathscr{C})^{\mathrm{op}}$ . commutative diagrams:

$$ {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces c} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces d} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces c^{\prime}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces d^{\prime}} $$

The formation of the twisted arrows category is natural in $\mathscr{C}$ ; every functor $F:\mathscr{C}\to\mathscr{D}$ induces a functor $\operatorname{Tw}(F):\operatorname{Tw}(\mathscr{C})\to\operatorname{Tw}(\mathscr{D})$ .

One has the twisted arrows formula for the space of natural transformations between a pair of functors $\mathscr{C}\to\mathscr{D}$ :

$$ \mathrm{Maps}(F,G)\simeq\lim_{\operatorname{Tw}(\mathscr{C})}\mathrm{Maps}_{\mathscr{D}}(F(c),G(c^{\prime})). $$

### A.1. Lax surjective functors

#### A.1.1.

We will say that a functor $F:\mathscr{C}\to\mathscr{D}$ is lax surjective if for every object $d\in\mathscr{D}$ there is an object $c\in\mathscr{C}$ and a map $F(c)\to d$ .

#### A.1.1 Proposition.

If $F:\mathscr{C}\to\mathscr{D}$ is essentially surjective, then $\operatorname{Tw}(F):\mathrm{Tw}(\mathscr{C})\to\mathrm{Tw}(\mathscr{D})$ is lax surjective.

# Unipotent Representations and the Categorical Trace of Frobenius

**Authors:** Wyatt Reeves

## Abstract

We give a new proof of the classification of unipotent representations for split finite groups of Lie type. To do this, we first construct an $(\infty,2)$ -categorification of Lusztig’s map from the Hecke algebra to the asymptotic algebra. Then we use the theory of weights to show that it induces an isomorphism after applying trace of Frobenius.
