$$ \mathscr{B}_{c,\leq n}^{{\mathbf{G}_{m}},\mathrm{ren}}=\Ind(\mathscr{B}_{c}^{{\mathbf{G}_{m}},\mathrm{dual}}\cap\mathscr{B}_{c,\leq n}^{\mathbf{G}_{m}}) $$

then this equips $\mathscr{B}_{c}^{\mathrm{ren}}$ with an $\mathbf{A}^{1}$ -action. It follows from Proposition 6.4.1 that the truncation functors of $\mathscr{B}_{c}^{\mathbf{G}_{m}}$ preserve $\mathscr{B}_{c}^{{\mathbf{G}_{m}},\mathrm{dual}}$ , so with respect to this $\mathbf{A}^{1}$ -action the (de-equivariantization of) un-ren is strictly $\mathbf{A}^{1}$ -equivariant. Moreover, the monoidal structure of $\mathscr{B}_{c}^{\mathrm{ren}}$ is strictly compatible with the action of $\mathbf{A}^{1}$ .

#### 6.4.3.

Let’s give an example of the difference between $\mathscr{B}_{c}$ and $\mathscr{B}_{c}^{\mathrm{ren}}$ : when $G=SL_{2}$ and $c=\left\{1\right\}$ , we saw in §4.1.6 that

$$ \mathscr{H}_{c}\simeq\QCoh(\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1}), $$

and this equivalence exchanges the monoidal structure on $\mathscr{H}_{c}$ with the convolution monoidal structure on $\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1}$ . Furthermore, for this cell $1_{c}=\gr_{0}(1_{c})$ , so $\mathscr{B}_{c}=\mathscr{H}_{c}$ . Note that the monoidal unit fails to be compact, even though it is of course dualizable (this is perhaps not so surprising, because the monoidal unit of $\mathscr{H}$ failed to be compact to begin with). On the other hand,

$$ \mathscr{B}_{c}^{\mathrm{ren}}\simeq\ICoh(\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1}), $$

again with the convolution monoidal structure. With respect to these identifications, the canonical monoidal functor $\mathscr{B}_{c}^{\mathrm{ren}}\to\mathscr{B}_{c}$ identifies with

$$ \Psi:\ICoh(\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1})\to\QCoh(\Omega\mathbf{A}^{1}). $$

#### Proposition 6.4.3.

$\mathrm{coact}:\mathscr{B}_{c}^{\mathrm{ren}}\to\QCoh(\mathbf{A}^{1})\otimes\mathscr{B}_{c}^{\mathrm{ren}}$ admits a continuous right adjoint.

#### Proof.

We can check this after taking ${\mathbf{G}_{m}}$ -invariants. The functor

$$ \mathrm{coact}^{\mathbf{G}_{m}}:\mathscr{B}_{c}^{{\mathbf{G}_{m}},\mathrm{ren}}\to\QCoh(\mathbf{A}^{1}/{\mathbf{G}_{m}})\otimes\mathscr{B}_{c}^{\mathrm{ren}} $$

is the composite

$$ \mathscr{B}_{c}^{{\mathbf{G}_{m}},\mathrm{ren}}\to\QCoh(\mathbf{A}^{1}/{\mathbf{G}_{m}})\otimes\mathscr{B}_{c}^{{\mathbf{G}_{m}},\mathrm{ren}}\xrightarrow{\id\otimes\mathrm{oblv}}\QCoh(\mathbf{A}^{1}/{\mathbf{G}_{m}})\otimes\mathscr{B}_{c}^{\mathrm{ren}} $$

where the first functor send $x\in\mathscr{B}_{c}^{{\mathbf{G}_{m}},\mathrm{ren}}$ to

$$ (\tau_{\leq n}x)\in\mathscr{B}_{c}^{{\mathbf{G}_{m}},\mathrm{ren},\mathrm{Fil}}\simeq\QCoh(\mathbf{A}^{1}/{\mathbf{G}_{m}})\otimes\mathscr{B}_{c}^{{\mathbf{G}_{m}},\mathrm{ren}}. $$

The second arrow in (32) has a continuous right adjoint by the rigidity of $\Rep({\mathbf{G}_{m}})$ , so it suffices to show that for any $x\in\mathscr{B}_{c}^{{\mathbf{G}_{m}},\mathrm{dual}}$ , the filtered object $(\tau_{\leq n}x)$ is compact as such. Since $\tau_{\leq n}x=0$ for $n\ll 0$ , its enough to show that $\gr_{\mathbin{\vbox{\hbox{\scalebox{.5}{$\bullet$}}}}}(x)$ is compact in $\Rep({\mathbf{G}_{m}})\otimes\mathscr{B}_{c}^{\mathrm{ren},{\mathbf{G}_{m}}}$ , and this follows from Proposition 6.4.1. ∎

#### 6.4.4.

By Proposition 6.1.4, the endomorphism $\mathrm{Frob}$ of $\mathscr{B}_{c}$ identifies with $\mathrm{act}_{\sqrt{q}}$ . In particular, $\mathrm{Frob}$ is $\mathbf{A}^{1}$ -equivariant. By §3.2.1, it follows that $HH(\mathscr{B}_{c};\mathrm{Frob})$ acquires a natural $\mathbf{A}^{1}$ -action.

#### Proposition 6.4.4.

Suppose that $\mathscr{C}$ and $\mathscr{D}$ are categories acted on by $\mathbf{A}^{1}$ . Suppose that there is an $\mathbf{A}^{1}$ -equivariant functor $\pi:\mathscr{D}\to\mathscr{C}$ which admits a fully-faithful (but not necessarily $\mathbf{A}^{1}$ -equivariant) left adjoint. If $\mathscr{C}$ is semisimple and the coaction functor

$$ \mathrm{coact}:\mathscr{D}\to\mathscr{D}\otimes\QCoh(\mathbf{A}^{1}) $$

is strongly continuous, then the endofunctor $\mathrm{act}_{0}$ of $\mathscr{C}$ is conservative.

#### Proof.

Slightly abusing notation, we will write $j^{*}$ and $j_{*}$ for the restriction functor

$$ \mathscr{C}\otimes\QCoh(\mathbf{A}^{1})\to\mathscr{C}\otimes\QCoh({\mathbf{G}_{m}}) $$

and its right adjoint, respectively. Similarly, we will write $\hat{\iota}^{*}$ and $\hat{\iota}_{+}$ for the restriction

$$ \mathscr{C}\otimes\QCoh(\mathbf{A}^{1})\to\mathscr{C}\otimes\QCoh(\mathbf{A}^{1})_{0} $$

and its left adjoint. We will also use this notation for the corresponding functors into and out of $\mathscr{D}\otimes\QCoh(\mathbf{A}^{1})$ , since it will be clear from context which categories we’re mapping out of.

To show that $\mathrm{act}_{0}$ is a conservative endomorphism of $\mathscr{C}$ , it suffices to show that for every simple object $x\in\mathscr{C}$ , $\mathrm{act}_{0}(x)\neq 0$ . Note that $i_{0}^{*}:\QCoh(\mathbf{A}^{1})_{0}\to\Vect$ admits a left adjoint whose image generates $\QCoh(\mathbf{A}^{1})_{0}$ . It follows that

$$ \mathscr{C}\otimes\QCoh(\mathbf{A}^{1})_{0}\xrightarrow{\id\otimes i_{0}^{*}}\mathscr{C} $$

is conservative, so if $\mathrm{act}_{0}(x)=0$ then $\hat{\iota}_{+}\hat{\iota}^{*}\mathrm{coact}_{\mathscr{C}}(x)=0$ .

We have an exact triangle

$$ \hat{\iota}_{+}\hat{\iota}^{*}\mathrm{coact}_{\mathscr{D}}\pi^{L}(x)\to\mathrm{coact}_{\mathscr{D}}\pi^{L}(x)\to j_{*}j^{*}\mathrm{coact}_{\mathscr{D}}\pi^{L}(x) $$

in $\mathscr{D}\otimes\QCoh(\mathbf{A}^{1})$ , and by assumption the middle term is compact ( $x$ is compact in $\mathscr{C}$ because it is simple; $\pi^{L}(x)$ is compact in $\mathscr{D}$ because $\pi^{L}$ has a continuous right adjoint). Because $\pi$ is $\mathbf{A}^{1}$ -equivariant, we know that $\pi^{L}$ is left-lax $\mathbf{A}^{1}$ -equivariant, and in particular ${\mathbf{G}_{m}}$ equivariant. By Proposition 6.3.0, it follows that

$$ j^{*}\circ\mathrm{coact}\circ\pi^{L}(x)\simeq\pi^{L}(x)\otimes\mathscr{O}_{\mathbf{G}_{m}}. $$

If $\hat{\iota}_{+}\hat{\iota}^{*}\mathrm{coact}_{\mathscr{C}}(x)=0$ then

$$ \hat{\iota}_{+}\hat{\iota}^{*}\mathrm{coact}_{\mathscr{D}}(x)\in\mathscr{C}^{\perp} $$

which would imply the vanishing of the boundary map

$$ j_{*}j^{*}\mathrm{coact}_{\mathscr{D}}\pi^{L}(x)\to\hat{\iota}_{+}\hat{\iota}^{*}\mathrm{coact}_{\mathscr{D}}\pi^{L}(x)[1]. $$

In particular, we would have

$$ \mathrm{coact}_{\mathscr{D}}\pi^{L}(x)\simeq\hat{\iota}_{+}\hat{\iota}^{*}\mathrm{coact}_{\mathscr{D}}\pi^{L}(x)\oplus\left(\pi^{L}(x)\otimes j_{*}(\mathscr{O}_{\mathbf{G}_{m}})\right). $$

This contradicts the compactness of $\mathrm{coact}_{\mathscr{D}}\pi^{L}(x)$ , because

$$ \pi^{L}(x)\otimes j_{*}(\mathscr{O}_{\mathbf{G}_{m}})\simeq\colim\pi^{L}(x)\otimes\mathscr{O}_{\mathbf{A}^{1}} $$

but the projection

$$ \mathrm{coact}_{\mathscr{D}}\pi^{L}(x)\to\pi^{L}(x)\otimes j_{*}(\mathscr{O}_{\mathbf{G}_{m}}) $$

doesn’t factor through any finite term of the colimit. ∎

#### Proposition 6.4.4.

The action of $\mathbf{A}^{1}$ on $HH(\mathscr{B}_{c};\mathrm{Frob})$ is trivializable.

#### Proof.

Since

$$ HH(\mathscr{B}_{c};\mathrm{Frob})\simeq\Rep(G(\mathbf{F}_{q}))^{\mathrm{unip}}_{c} $$

is semisimple, by Proposition 6.3.0 it suffices to show that the endofunctor $\mathrm{act}_{0}$ of $HH(\mathscr{B}_{c};\mathrm{Frob})$ is conservative. By Construction 2.2.2 and Proposition 2.2.2, we have a diagram

$$ HH(\textrm{un-ren};\mathrm{Frob})^{L}:HH(\mathscr{B}_{c};\mathrm{Frob})\rightleftarrows HH(\mathscr{B}_{c}^{\mathrm{ren}};\mathrm{Frob}):HH(\textrm{un-ren};\mathrm{Frob}) $$

exhibiting $HH(\mathscr{B}_{c};\mathrm{Frob})$ as a coreflective subcategory of $HH(\mathscr{B}_{c}^{\mathrm{ren}};\mathrm{Frob})$ . By §3.2.1 the functor $\pi=HH(\textrm{un-ren};\mathrm{Frob})$ is $\mathbf{A}^{1}$ -equivariant. By Proposition 6.4.3 and Proposition 3.2.1 the coaction functor for $HH(\mathscr{B}_{c}^{\mathrm{ren}};\mathrm{Frob})$ is strongly continuous, so we may apply Proposition 6.4.4 with $\mathscr{C}=HH(\mathscr{B}_{c};\mathrm{Frob})$ , $\mathscr{D}=HH(\mathscr{B}_{c}^{\mathrm{ren}};\mathrm{Frob})$ , and $\pi$ the functor between them. ∎

#### Proposition 6.4.4.

$$ HH(\mathscr{B}_{c};\mathrm{Frob})\simeq HH(\mathscr{J}_{c};\id) $$

#### Proof.

By Proposition 6.4.4 and Proposition 3.2.1 we know that

$$ HH(\mathscr{B}_{c};\mathrm{Frob})\simeq HH(\mathscr{B}_{c};\mathrm{Frob})^{\mathbf{A}^{1}}\simeq HH(\mathscr{B}_{c}^{\mathbf{A}^{1}};\mathrm{Frob}). $$

By Proposition 5.2.1 we know that $\mathscr{B}^{\mathbf{A}^{1}}\simeq\mathscr{J}_{c}$ (in fact, this is true as a monoidal category by Proposition 5.3.1), and by Proposition 6.1.4 we know that $\mathrm{Frob}$ acts trivially on $\mathscr{J}_{c}$ , so the result follows. ∎

#### Theorem 6.4.4.

$$ HH(\mathscr{H}_{c};\mathrm{Frob})\simeq HH(\mathscr{J}_{c};\id). $$

#### Proof.

This follows immediately from what we have already proved:

$$ HH(\mathscr{H}_{c};\mathrm{Frob})\overset{(\textrm{\lx@cref{creftypecap~refnum}{prop:hh-hc-equals-hh-bc}})}{\simeq}HH(\mathscr{B}_{c};\mathrm{Frob})\overset{(\textrm{\lx@cref{creftypecap~refnum}{prop:hh-bc-equals-hh-jc}})}{\simeq}HH(\mathscr{J}_{c};\id). $$

∎

### 6.5. Proof of Theorem 1.1.4

#### 6.5.1.

If $\Gamma$ is a finite group and $k$ is an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, then

$$ H^{3}(\Gamma;k^{\times})\simeq H^{3}(\Gamma;\mu_{\infty})\simeq H^{4}(\Gamma;\mathbf{Z}). $$

Given a cocycle $\omega\in H^{3}(\Gamma;k^{\times})$ , we get an isomorphism class of maps

$$ B\Gamma\to B^{3}{\mathbf{G}_{m}}. $$

Every map $B\Gamma\to B^{3}{\mathbf{G}_{m}}$ may be upgraded to a pointed map, and the space of pointed structures is connected (because we are working over an algebraically closed field). Applying $\Omega$ , we obtain an $\mathbf{E}_{1}$ -map $\Gamma\to B^{2}{\mathbf{G}_{m}}$ , well-defined up to isomorphism. Pulling back the universal gerbe on $B^{2}{\mathbf{G}_{m}}$ , we obtain a monoidal category $\Vect_{\Gamma,\omega}$ . This category is isomorphic to $\QCoh(\Gamma)$ as a plain category, but the associativity constraint of its monoidal structure is modified according to $\omega$ .

The $(\infty,2)$ -category

$$ \Vect_{\Gamma,\omega}\textrm{-mod} $$

is fully-dualizable, and corresponds under the cobordism hypothesis to a 3d TQFT which is called Dijkgraaf-Witten theory (with gauge group $\Gamma$ and level $\omega$ ). For more information, see [Qui98].

#### Theorem 6.5.1.

The category $\Rep(G(\mathbf{F}_{q}))^{\mathrm{unip}}$ admits a direct sum decomposition indexed by two-sided cells

$$ \Rep(G(\mathbf{F}_{q}))^{\mathrm{unip}}\simeq\bigoplus_{c}\Rep(G(\mathbf{F}_{q}))^{\mathrm{unip}}_{c} $$

such that

$$ \Rep(G(\mathbf{F}_{q}))^{\mathrm{unip}}_{c}\simeq\QCoh_{\mathscr{G}}(A_{c}/A_{c}) $$

for a finite group $A_{c}$ and gerbe $\mathscr{G}$ .

#### Proof.

By §6.2.1,

$$ \Rep(G(\mathbf{F}_{q}))^{\mathrm{unip}}\simeq HH(\mathscr{H};\mathrm{Frob}). $$

Therefore Construction 2.2.2 implies that the system of semiorthogonal decompositions of $\mathscr{H}$ defined in §4.1.5 gives rise to a system of semiorthogonal decompositions of $\Rep(G(\mathbf{F}_{q}))^{\mathrm{unip}}$ . Every semiorthogonal decomposition of a semisimple category is a direct sum decomposition, so we obtain

$$ \Rep(G(\mathbf{F}_{q}))^{\mathrm{unip}}\simeq\bigoplus_{c}\Rep(G(\mathbf{F}_{q}))^{\mathrm{unip}}_{c} $$

where

$$ \Rep(G(\mathbf{F}_{q}))^{\mathrm{unip}}_{c}=HH(\mathscr{H}_{c};\mathrm{Frob}). $$

Applying Theorem 6.4.4, we know that

$$ HH(\mathscr{H}_{c};\mathrm{Frob})\simeq HH(\mathscr{J}_{c};\id). $$

As explained in §1.2.9, [LO14, Theorem 5.1] implies the existence of an equivalence

$$ \mathscr{J}_{c}\textrm{-mod}\simeq\Vect_{A_{c},\omega} $$

for some finite group $A_{c}$ and some 3-cocycle $\omega$ . Now the result follows from [Fre94, Wil08], which show that

$$ \tr(\id;\Vect_{A_{c},\omega})\simeq\QCoh_{\mathscr{G}}(A_{c}/A_{c}) $$

for some gerbe $\mathscr{G}$ defined in terms of $\omega$ . ∎

#### 6.5.2.

In fact, it is known that the gerbe $\mathscr{G}$ appearing in Theorem 6.5.1 may always be trivialized. This is because case-by-case calculations show that for all but three two-sided cells (one in type $E_{7}$ and two in type $E_{8}$ ), $\omega$ is trivial. These three cells with nontrivial $\omega$ are called exceptional, and for all three exceptional cells $A_{c}=\mathbf{Z}/2$ . For the non-exceptional cells, the triviality of $\omega$ implies the triviality of $\mathscr{G}$ . On the other hand, for the exceptional cells,

$$ A_{c}/A_{c}\simeq B(\mathbf{Z}/2)\sqcup B(\mathbf{Z}/2) $$

and every gerbe on $B(\mathbf{Z}/2)$ is trivializable.
